title: Install your web app on a phone and share it

steps.title: What we'll do today
steps.html:
The timer from App 1 still lives only on your computer. Today you'll put it online, install it like an app on your phone's home screen, and share an address anyone can use.

timer folderuploadGitHubturn on PagesYour app's addressAdd to Home ScreenPhone app
  • Time: 20 minutes
  • You need: the timer folder from App 1, a GitHub account (if not, see the sign-up step in Phone 2), and a phone
  • Cost: free

New to GitHub? Try GitHub at a glance (10 min) first.

steps.title: Make it fit the home screen
steps.html:
You'll make the app name and icon show on the home screen, and have it open without an address bar, like an app. A web app set up this way is called a PWA (installable web app).

In the Code tab, continue the App 1 chat, or open a new chat with the Practice folder and send this. Check the create-file cards and click Allow.
steps.code: Make the web app in the timer folder open like an app when added to a phone's home screen. Name it 'Workout timer', and create a stopwatch icon on a blue background (PNG) and a manifest file

check.q: Are there a manifest file and an icon image file in the timer folder?

steps.title: If the icon isn't created
steps.html:
• To make a PNG it may ask to install a tool (e.g. Pillow). Check what it installs and allow it, or say "Make an SVG and skip the PNG." (iPhone uses a PNG icon)
  • Have a picture you like? Put it in the timer folder and say "Use this picture as the icon."

steps.title: Make a public repository on GitHub and upload
steps.html:
1. github.com → + at the top right → New repository.
  2. Name: timer · Public · tick Add a README file → Create repository.
  3. On the repository page: Add file → Upload files.
  4. On your computer, open the timer folder and select all the files inside, then drag them in.
  5. Click Commit changes at the bottom.
This time it's Public. A free web address needs a public repository, so anyone can read the files. Never put names, phone numbers, passwords or API keys in it. (Leave my-notes from Phone 2 private.)
steps.alt: Dragging the files inside the timer folder onto GitHub's Upload files screen

check.q: Can you see index.html in the timer repository?

steps.title: If uploading doesn't work
steps.html:
• Dragging the whole timer folder adds an extra level. index.html must show on the repository's front page; if not, upload just the files inside.
  • Dragging is hard on a phone. Do this step in a computer browser.

steps.title: Turn on GitHub Pages and get your app's address
steps.html:
GitHub Pages is a free feature that serves a repository's files as a website.

  1. timer repository → Settings → Pages on the left.
  2. Source: Deploy from a branch · Branch: main · / (root) → Save.
  3. Wait 1–2 minutes and refresh: Your site is live at https://your-id.github.io/timer/ appears at the top.
  4. Click that address and check the timer opens.
steps.alt: Choosing main and Save in Settings → Pages, with the site address shown

check.q: Does the timer open at https://your-id.github.io/timer/?

steps.title: If no address appears, or you get a 404
steps.html:
• The first time takes a few minutes. Refresh again shortly. The repository's Actions tab shows progress.
  • 404: check index.html sits right on the repository's front page (not inside a folder).
  • If Pages shows an upgrade notice, the repository is Private. Settings → bottom Change visibility → Public.

steps.title: Install it on your phone's home screen
steps.html:
Open your app's address (https://your-id.github.io/timer/) in your phone's browser. Sending it to yourself in a message makes this easy.

  • Android (Chrome): ⋮ at the top right → Add to Home screen (or Install app) → Add.
  • iPhone (Safari): Share (□↑) at the bottom → Add to Home Screen → Add.

Tap the Workout timer icon on your home screen. It opens like an app, with no address bar.
steps.alt: A Workout timer icon on the phone's home screen

check.q: Does it open from the home screen icon, and does the timer work?

steps.title: If Add to Home Screen is missing or odd
steps.html:
• On iPhone, only Safari can add to the home screen.
  • If the icon shows a letter instead of a picture, ask Claude "Add an iPhone home screen icon (apple-touch-icon) too", then upload the changed files again.
  • No sound? Check the phone isn't on silent.

steps.title: How to update · be careful
steps.html:
1. Tell Claude on your computer what to change, and allow it (like App 1).
  2. Upload files again to the GitHub timer repository. Same-named files are replaced.
  3. After 1–2 minutes, close and reopen the app on your phone.

Once you're comfortable, you can have Claude edit the timer repository directly and merge via a PR, like Phone 3.

  • Public repository: anyone can read what you upload. No personal data, passwords or API keys.
  • Records stay on each phone: if you add a history feature, it's saved only in each user's phone browser. Collecting it on a server is a bigger topic.
  • Don't copy others: don't reuse another app's name, pictures or music.

steps.title: 🎉 App practice 2 done! Your app is on your phone
steps.html:
The app you built with words now has a web address and lives on your phone's home screen. Share the address and family and friends can use it too.

Three things to remember

  1. GitHub Pages turns repository files into a free website. It's public, so anyone can see it.
  2. With a manifest and icon, it installs on the home screen like an app.
  3. To update: change it with Claude → upload again.

Building with just your phone, no computer, is App 3; an Android app (APK) is App 4.
